options: [Ru(bpy)3]2+
[MnO4]-

questions.question: According to the mutual exclusion rule in vibrational spectroscopy, which statement correctly describes the behavior of a centrosymmetric molecule like carbon dioxide (CO2)?
options: A vibrational mode can be simultaneously IR-active and Raman-active if it preserves the center of inversion.
The symmetric stretching mode is IR-active and Raman-inactive.
The asymmetric stretching mode is IR-active and Raman-inactive.
The degenerate bending modes are Raman-active and IR-inactive.

questions.question: In the Wittig reaction, which combination of ylide type and reaction parameter preferentially yields the (E)-alkene product?
options: Unstabilized ylides forming an oxaphosphetane under irreversible, kinetically controlled conditions.
Stabilized ylides (e.g., ester-substituted) undergoing reversible oxaphosphetane formation leading to thermodynamic control.
Non-stabilized ylides in the presence of excess lithium salts forcing rapid collapse of the betaine intermediate.
Unstabilized ylides reacted in polar aprotic solvents at low temperatures.

questions.question: In X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS), core-level electrons are ejected by monochromatic X-ray photons. How does the measured binding energy (Eb) of a core electron in a transition metal atom typically change as the oxidation state of the metal increases?
options: The binding energy increases because reduced electron-electron screening increases the effective nuclear charge felt by core electrons.
The binding energy decreases because the increased positive charge stabilizes the kinetic energy of the ejected photoelectron.
The binding energy remains unchanged because core orbitals do not participate in chemical bonding or oxidation state changes.
The binding energy decreases because higher formal oxidation states pull valence electron density inward, shielding core orbitals.

questions.question: In the Cossee-Arlman mechanism for the stereospecific polymerization of propene using a heterogeneous TiCl3/AlEt3 Ziegler-Natta catalyst, what is the key structural feature of the active catalytic center?
options: A tetrahedral Ti(II) species bearing a terminal oxo ligand.
A pentacoordinate Ti(IV) center with two vacant coordination sites in a trans configuration.
A square planar Ti(IV) complex with bridging hydride ligands supplied by triethylaluminum.
An octahedral Ti(III) center featuring a vacant coordination site cis to the growing polymer chain.
